extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS 2020 reviewers (and area chairs / senior area chairs assisting reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and scoring rubric for reviewers assigned to NeurIPS 2020 submissions, covering reviewer responsibilities, review content, scoring (overall and confidence), confidentiality, conflicts, and procedural requirements (CMT/TPMS/OpenReview).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer responsibilities (assignment and duties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are typically assigned around 4-6 submissions and are responsible for reviewing submissions, reading author responses, discussing submissions and author responses with other reviewers and area chairs (ACs), and helping make decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewing process is double blind at the level of reviewers and ACs. There are no physical meetings; discussions take place via CMT. Reviewer identities are visible to other reviewers, ACs and SACs. After decisions reviews and meta-reviews will be made public (reviewer and SAC/AC identities remain anonymous). As soon as reviewers are notified, they should log in to CMT to check for conflicts and area fit. If uncomfortable reviewing, fill out a note in CMT and communicate to the AC immediately because it takes time to find alternates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check and declare conflicts promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must log in to CMT to check for conflicts as soon as assigned and ensure papers fall within their expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not comfortable, fill out a note in CMT and notify the AC immediately. Keep domain conflicts in CMT up to date to prevent improper assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer evaluation by ACs (review quality scoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: ACs will evaluate the quality of each review using three scores: “exceeded expectations”, “met expectations,” and “failed to meet expectations.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Top-performing reviewers (top 8%) awarded free registrations; next 30% have registrations reserved. Lowest-scoring reviewers may not be invited in future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: It is okay to be unavailable briefly, but reviewers must notify ACs if they will be unavailable for longer or during key windows (e.g., discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to emails promptly and respect deadlines. If you will be unavailable for more than a few days, especially during discussion, inform ACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professionalism, fairness, and non-discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Write thoughtful and constructive reviews and accord with the NeurIPS code of conduct. Avoid subtle discrimination and inappropriate language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: avoid comments that imply the author is 'foreign' (e.g., replace 'have a native English speaker proofread' with 'have your submission proof-read for English style and grammar issues'). Be professional and polite; don't be dismissive.

rubrics_metrics.name: No informal discussion of assigned submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do NOT talk to other reviewers, ACs, or SACs about submissions assigned to you without prior approval from your AC; do not discuss your own submissions or those with which you have a conflict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary contact for discussions should be the corresponding AC for that submission. Other reviewers/ACs/SACs may have conflicts with the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep everything relating to the review process confidential and do not use ideas, code, or results from submissions in your own work until they are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not distribute submissions (code or ideas) without program chairs' approval. Code submitted for reviewing cannot be distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing is double blind at the level of reviewers and ACs; authors must anonymize submissions (no names, affiliations, acknowledgements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assigned a submission that is not adequately anonymized, contact the corresponding AC. Under no circumstances should you attempt to find out author identities (e.g., via Google/arXiv). If you accidentally find out, do not divulge identities and do not let identities influence decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary material policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit up to 100MB of supplementary material (proofs, derivations, data, source code) in PDF or ZIP format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer responsibility is to read and review the submission itself; examining supplementary material is at the reviewer's discretion. Because main submissions are short, reviewers may wish to consult supplementary material before criticizing insufficient details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executing submitted code and visiting links (security)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted code may contain security vulnerabilities. Reviewers planning to run code should do so in a secure environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended environments: (1) Docker container, (2) Virtual Machine image (VirtualBox/VMWare), or (3) network-isolated cloud instance. Be cautious about web links that may log IP addresses or contain vulnerabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and page limit compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are limited to eight content pages (including figures/tables) in the NeurIPS 'submission' style; additional pages allowed only for (a) broader impact discussion and (b) references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must use the NeurIPS 2020 LaTeX style file. If you see style or page limit violations (e.g., decreasing margins or font size), notify the AC immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions identical or substantially similar to papers submitted to or published in other archival venues (or other NeurIPS submissions) should be deemed dual submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be distinct and sufficiently substantial. 'Slicing' contributions too thinly may qualify as dual submissions. If you suspect dual submission, contact the corresponding AC. See Call for Papers and FAQ for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of substantive review content
rubrics_metrics.description: Review content is the primary means by which ACs, SACs, and program chairs make decisions and how authors understand decisions; provide detailed, informative reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short, superficial reviews that venture uninformed opinions are worse than no review. For rejected submissions, reviews should help authors improve; for accepted submissions, help authors with camera-ready improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form: Summary and contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the paper motivation, key contributions and achievements in a paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps ACs and authors see misunderstandings. Contributions that warrant publication may be theoretical, methodological, algorithmic, empirical, bridge papers, or critical analyses. See Examples of Review Content for exemplar phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form: Strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the strengths of the work, e.g., soundness of claims, empirical evaluation, significance, novelty, and relevance to the NeurIPS community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List concrete strengths (e.g., correct theoretical claims, solid experiments). Cite relevant prior works precisely when comparing significance/novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form: Weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the limitations of the work along the same axes as strengths (soundness, significance, novelty, relevance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be detailed, specific, and polite; avoid vague subjective complaints. Remember you are evaluating scientific contribution, not your personal interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form: Correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the claims and methods are correct and whether empirical methodology is correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorrect claims or methodology are primary grounds for rejection. Be detailed and specific in identifying errors and fully motivate criticisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Rate the clarity of exposition and whether the paper is well written and organized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give examples of parts needing revision and suggestions to improve clarity; note missing equation numbers, incorrect appendix references, or repetitive paragraphs as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form: Relation to prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain whether the submission clearly discusses how it differs from previous contributions and whether the related work explains differences (not merely listing works).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are excused for not knowing all non-refereed work (e.g., arXiv). Papers appearing less than two months before submission deadline are considered contemporaneous; authors are not obligated to make detailed comparisons to such papers for the submission (but camera-ready should address them).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form: Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether there are enough details to reproduce major results of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not reproducible, list lack of reproducibility among weaknesses. Indicate whether details, code, or supplementary material provide necessary replication information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form: Additional feedback and questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide any additional comments, suggestions for improvement, or direct questions for the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this space for constructive suggestions, requests for clarifications (e.g., 'I would like to see results of experiment X' or parameter settings), and other feedback not captured above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form: Overall score (10–1) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Score should reflect your assessment of the submission's contributions and not be adjusted to conference acceptance rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Score meanings: 10 = Top 5% of accepted NeurIPS papers (groundbreaking); 9 = Top 15% (excellent); 8 = Top 50% accepted (very good); 7 = good (accept; would not be upset if rejected); 6 = marginally above acceptance threshold (lean accept); 5 = marginally below acceptance threshold (lean reject); 4 = okay but not good enough (reject); 3 = clear reject; 2 = surprised it was submitted (strong reject); 1 = trivial/wrong/already known. Use these descriptions to calibrate numeric ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review form: Confidence score (5–1) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Report your confidence in the assessment on a 5-point scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 5 = absolutely certain / very familiar with related work; 4 = confident but not absolutely certain; 3 = fairly confident (possible unfamiliarity or un-checked math); 2 = willing to defend but likely unfamiliar or didn't check details; 1 = educated guess (not in area or difficult to understand).

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader impact statement adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the authors adequately addressed the broader impact of their work, including potential negative ethical and societal implications?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer: Yes, No, or Only partially. Authors are required to include a statement of potential broader impact discussing both positive and negative outcomes. Indicate whether the broader impact section was adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging potential ethical concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the submission raise potential ethical concerns (methods, applications, data that create/reinforce unfair bias or aim to harm)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer Yes or No and briefly explain if Yes. This rating is independent of paper quality; if AC shares concern, dedicated ethics reviewers may further review. Your duty is to flag papers needing additional ethics review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior reviewing of the same work disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether you have previously reviewed or area chaired a version of this work for another archival venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yes or No. This helps ACs/SACs put your review in context; ACs may access a resubmission statement and decide whether to share it with reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agree to abide by the NeurIPS code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must agree to abide by the NeurIPS code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The code of conduct is linked (https://neurips.cc/public/CodeOfConduct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to area chair
rubrics_metrics.description: A text field for comments that should be kept confidential from authors, e.g., blunt criticisms or explicit comparisons to other submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this for comparisons or criticisms not intended for authors. If you accidentally find author identities, do not divulge them. Sensitive criticisms may go here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must read and (if appropriate) respond to each author response during the author response phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not fair to ignore author responses. Update your review to indicate you read the response and whether you agree/disagree with it. Be specific rather than saying only 'I have read the author response and my opinion remains the same'—explain why it remains the same or what was not addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion phase participation
rubrics_metrics.description: After author response, the AC will initiate a discussion to encourage reviewers to reach consensus; reviewers should engage actively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion is important for borderline submissions and conflicting assessments. Consider other reviewers' points and change your mind if appropriate, but not required. Consensus is valuable and usually followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of review content and exemplars
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidelines provide many concrete example excerpts illustrating how to write constructive strengths/weaknesses, and examples for Quality, Clarity, Originality, Significance, and Contribution statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exemplar quotes and formats to guide your own comments (e.g., describe experiments, theoretical contributions, specific technical issues, and concrete suggested fixes). Examples include sample phrasing for technical critiques, clarity issues, missing related work, and evaluation of significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of submission system (CMT) for reviews and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: All reviews must be submitted via the NeurIPS 2020 CMT site; reviewers may revise reviews as needed. Use same email for author and reviewer roles if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reply directly to emails sent by CMT. Use the 'email meta-reviewer' and 'email senior meta-reviewer' links in CMT to send emails. Check spam folders for CMT emails and whitelist email@msr-cmt.org.
